column1: # ceiling-overrides.tsv — per-suite PER-TEST TIMEOUT ceilings, as DATA.
# Enforced by:  monitor/watcher/run-tests.sh  (run_one, _rt_ceiling_for)
# Asserted by:  monitor/watcher/test-run-tests-accounting-verdict.sh
# WHY THIS FILE EXISTS (your-org/nexus-code#992). A suite whose wall time sits
# just under the run's ceiling does not FAIL — it FLAPS, and a flap is worse
# than a clean red on every axis that matters: it is non-deterministic, so it
# does not reproduce on the first re-run and looks like it "went away"; it
# carries NO diagnostic content, because `TIMEOUT at the ceiling` names no
# assertion and no behaviour; and it is re-diagnosed from scratch every time it
# fires, by someone with no reason to suspect the ceiling. Measured: roughly an
# hour of one session, including a foreground probe that blew its own limit
# before the cause was found.
# THE NUMBER IS A PROPERTY OF THE SUITE, NOT OF THE WORKFLOW. Raising the
# workflow-level ceiling would hide the flap for every suite at once, including
# suites that are slow because they are BROKEN. A per-suite ceiling says
# "THIS suite legitimately takes this long", which is a claim someone can check
# against the row's own measurement, and it leaves the global default free to
# stay tight for everything else.
# COLUMNS   suite-basename <TAB> ceiling-seconds <TAB> measured-wall <TAB> why
# HOW TO PICK THE CEILING: at least 2x the MAXIMUM observed wall, never 2x a
# single sample. Column 3 therefore records the max of a distribution, not one
# measurement — #992's own reopen is the cautionary case, where a single 570.21s
# sample sat 43s below a 613.23s member of the same distribution on byte-identical
# code. A row whose ceiling is only a little above its measurement has not fixed
# the flap, it has moved it.
# A ROW IS NOT A LICENCE TO BE SLOW. `run-tests.sh` still prints the
# CEILING-ADJACENT census (>=NEXUS_CEILING_ADJACENT_PCT of the ceiling in use),
# now measured against the OVERRIDDEN ceiling, so a suite that grows into its
# new headroom says so on every run instead of going quiet.
# ── THE FAMILY, recorded because the fifth will otherwise be rediscovered from
# scratch (fix 3 of #992). Only the first is given an override here; the other
# three are load-sensitive under parallelism rather than ceiling-adjacent on
# their own, and an unmeasured override would be a number nobody can check.
#   test-run-tests-bounded.sh      n=8 on BYTE-IDENTICAL code, from #992's
#                                  Range 524.85-613.23, TWO OF EIGHT over 600.
#                                  Structurally the worst case: it is a test OF
#                                  the bounded runner, so it works by RUNNING
#                                  SUITES and inherits every one of their load
#                                  sensitivities multiplied together.
#                                  NOT A FLAKE AND NOT A DETERMINISTIC OVERRUN,
#                                  and the reopen refutes both readings with the
#                                  same data: 580.71s at loadavg 37.66 PASSED
#                                  where 600.01s at loadavg 37.08 TIMED OUT, so
#                                  load does not predict the side. What is true
#                                  is narrower — 600 is a ceiling set INSIDE the
#                                  suite's own runtime distribution. That is why
#                                  the remedy is to move the ceiling OUT of the
#                                  distribution rather than to retry: a retry
#                                  burns ten minutes to re-roll the same die.
#   test-guards-for-diff.sh        A ~25-28 MINUTE suite, and the per-test ceiling a
#                                  caller picks sits INSIDE its distribution
#                                  (your-org/nexus-code#1474, local form). Measured
#                                  dedicated Slurm cores at --jobs 6 (this repo's
#                                  test-evidence bundle, ref 76abc6a5); 1668.60 s
#                                  PASS against 1800 (92%, run-tests.sh itself
#                                  flagged it CEILING-ADJACENT) at ref 4825e3e1,
#                                  36 cpus, load ~40, --jobs 4 — reported by the
#                                  `promote` worker, cited as such; and TIMEOUT-
#                                  killed four of four times at a 900 s ceiling on
#                                  the same quiet box (censored: the true wall is
#                                  > 900 each time). NOT a hang: it completes. It
#                                  multiplies a ~2-minute primitive (one full
#                                  `guards-for-diff` population sweep, ~17
#                                  invocations, cost linear in the guard count,
#                                  which only grows), so a row only buys time —
#                                  the lever is the invocation count or the
#                                  primitive's cost (#1474 thread, w232 item 2).
#                                  The row is 3600: >= 2x the MAX observed
#                                  (1668.60), never 2x a single sample.
#   test-idle-probe.sh             310/0 standalone; flakes under --jobs 4 + load.
#   test-proc-kill-authorized.sh   red under a parallel sweep, GREEN isolated.
#   test-assertion-ledger.sh       `dev` ITSELF failed it while a bundle passed
#                                  it in the same batch; 0/8 at both refs run
#                                  sequentially. That one cannot be explained by
#                                  anything the change did, which is the
#                                  strongest evidence the class is LOAD.
test-run-tests-bounded.sh
